inflection.note: Read from the registry, the silver and bronze listings, mirror_schemas.py DECLARED (orion transactions 31 names, positions 59) and the converter's transTypeId dictionary in convert_transactions_to_silver.py, as code rules only. Not measured: the transTypeId vocabulary as data, the value semantics and signs against real rows, whether costBasis is a lot-level or a position-level cost, and the earliest account record. Two writers carry the Orion transactions: the canonical mirror writer (DECLARED names) and the legacy flat writer (31 bronze names plus 11 carried Custom Report columns and trans_type_desc); the mapping uses the names both carry.

notes: base_commit is the HEAD read before the first commit of this order (git rev-parse HEAD in the worktree).

The shape: 19 distinct columns in ARROW_ACTIVITY. contributions and withdrawals are the positive and the absolute negative of the per-custodian-day net external flow (activity_row); realized is the realized gain of lots closed in the interval; unrealized_change is the change in the summed unrealized gain plus inkind_departure_gain; income is the net of income_gross, income_fee_admin and income_withheld_tax (the three signed negative components are carried beside it); beginning_value and ending_value are the custodian whole-account value V (net_mv_plus_cash plus margin_balance, per the sources.json comment); identity_gap and rounding_allowance are the identity check; coverage names why a figure is null or whether the identity is graded.

The 49F source of the producer: exactly one custody source is read (compute_local refuses a count other than one at account_activity_lots.py line 1040-1041; the reporting-gold handler refuses it at handler.py line 222-224). sources.json declares one custody entry (schwab_08335338) with the lot_source object. No Black Diamond or Orion entry exists.

Cottonwood and Inflection landed transaction tables are read by prefix listing only (list-objects-v2 with a delimiter, partition names and counts). No object body, no head-object of a manifest, no row count was read. A registry _SUCCESS or manifest key was not looked for.

Bucket names come from opal_naming.address() output for the silver tier (the shared home for FIRM tenancy), not typed: the listed prefixes are the canonical silver prefixes of opal-data-assets. The legacy locations are the registry aliases spelled in scopes.json (opal-data-cot, opal-data-inf).

Cottonwood _s2 prefixes (fact_transactions_s2, fact_realized_s2, fact_unrealized_s2, fact_holdings_s2) are the Black Diamond Timestamps section (mirror_schemas.py TIMESTAMPS_SECTION: two headerless columns). They are not second transaction tables.

Cottonwood's transaction rules were read from the cot code (c00_flow_ledger.py: the rename map lines 108-129 and the class ladder lines 144-240; a05_ref_txn_classification.py lines 55-77). Those are code rules, not measured against rows.

Inflection history: the canonical silver fact_transactions starts 2026-05-12, while the legacy flat silver/transactions history starts 2020-05-26 with 1656 files; 145 of those legacy files fall on or after 2026-05-12. The two spans differ; the mapping uses the canonical 145-partition span as the landed source and the legacy history is recorded as a surprise row.

Account key spaces: the 49F account_id is zero-padded to 10 (sources.json account_id_zero_pad). The Cottonwood AccountID carries a firm-instance prefix, per the scopes.json note on the z09 master (measured there at 2026-09-24, not re-measured here). The Inflection accountId is int64. A producer build must reconcile the three key spaces; this order compared none of them.

Surprise rows filed: IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W371-S1 (Inflection history in two places with different spans), S2 (account key spaces differ from the 49F key), S3 (the CTO's same-shape premise fails for realized and in-kind on Inflection: no lot feed), S4 (two writers with two column sets for the Orion transactions table).

The Cottonwood realized, unrealized and holdings tables are landed under the canonical silver home with the names of the BD vendor schema, so the Cottonwood lot adapter is a declaration to write (a sources.json entry with lot_source) and not a new feed.

functions_invoked 0, sign_ins_made 0, aws_writes_made 0, rows_written 0, figures_written 0, vendor_requests_sent 0. The AWS calls were sts get-caller-identity and s3api list-objects-v2 with a delimiter, all read-only.
Client data rule: this record carries column names, partition counts, dates and the mapping only. No account id, client id, amount, transaction value or object key is recorded.
